## (1) The previous check's failing lines

### LINE 1: Q198, the first test (`bench/test/tiers/exec.test.ts`, busy child): FIXED and PINNED, tests only. CONFIRMED

**Source read.** The seat read `docs/M0-FIX-QUEUE.md` row Q198 whole (grep `^| Q198 `), J787 (4) and (5), `exec.ts`
whole and the test. `spawnExecutor` takes the CPU time from the second line of the shell's `times` builtin (the
children's user and system time). It has no source change: `exec.ts` is byte-equal to its index blob.

**The new test.** The planted child spins until its OWN `process.cpuUsage()` (user + system) reaches
`BUSY_CPU_MS` = 250. It then idles `IDLE_MS` = 400 with `setTimeout` and prints `done true cpu <ms>`. The test asserts:

* exit 0 and the output line;
* the child's own reading ≥ 250;
* `cpuMs` ≥ the child's reading − 30;
* `wallMs` ≥ 400;
* `cpuMs` ≤ `wallMs` − 200;
* one pid reported, and a second child's exit code 3 passed through.

The exit-code, output and pid assertions stay. Load stretches the time a child takes to burn 250 ms of CPU, but it can
never lower the CPU used. So both bounds are facts of the child (PLAUSIBLE by reading; CONFIRMED by the load runs
below).

The 30 ms tolerance is sound. On Linux, dash's `times` (`/bin/sh -> dash`) prints `times(2)` clock ticks at 100 Hz:
user and system are each truncated to 10 ms, so at most 20 ms under. CPU used after the child's last reading (its
print and exit) only adds to the executor's figure (PLAUSIBLE). Mutant E4 shows the effect directly: the executor read
240 ms where the child said 251.4 ms.

**Mutants.** All ran in the mirror, each against NEAR (`vitest run --maxWorkers=1 bench/test/tiers`); the clean run
was 72 / 72. Every mutant is red, and each first assertion is quoted:

| id | mutant (`exec.ts`) | result |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | the wall-clock reported as CPU time (`cpuMs: wallMs`) | red: 'expected 660.678828 to be less than or equal to 460.678…' |
| E2 | CPU time reported as 0 | red: 'expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 221.705' |
| E3 | the shell's OWN `times` line (line 1) read | red: busy test 'expected 0 …' and the parseTimes test |
| E4 | CPU time halved | red: 'expected 120.0… to be greater than or equal to 221.452' |
| E5 | system time dropped (user only) | red: 'expected 110 …' and parseTimes |
| E6 | `onSpawn` never called | red: 'expected +0 to be 1' (the pid assertion) |
| E7 | CPU time reported as the wall-clock | red: 'expected 260 to be greater than or equal to 400' |
| E8 | exit code always 0 | red: 'expected +0 to be 3' (and the missing-program test, 127) |
| E9 | CPU over-reported by 250 ms | red: 'expected 510 to be less than or equal to 474.2…' |

The brief's two named mutants are E1 (wall-clock as CPU time) and E2 (0). Both are red. CONFIRMED.

**Load.** The command, run in the mirror (identical to the tree):

```
corepack pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=1 bench/test/tiers/exec.test.ts -t "measures a busy child"
```

It was run 20 times alone, then 20 times beside six busy loops (`( while :; do :; done ) &` × 6, started 20 s before
the first run and killed after the last; `kill -0` confirmed all six gone).

| condition | passed | load average |
|---|---|---|
| alone | 20 / 20 | 0.91 – 1.31 |
| beside six busy loops on the four cores | 20 / 20 | 2.98 rising to 6.50 |

That is 40 of 40 green. CONFIRMED.

### LINE 2: Q175 (d), `runTier` and `fallback: true` outside tier:pr: FIXED and PINNED. CONFIRMED

**Source read.** The seat read Q175 whole and Q151 whole (each by its own grep), N-13 of this item's notes, `runner.ts`
whole and `index.ts` whole.

**The guard.** `runTier` throws when `opts.fallback === true && manifest.tier !== 'pr'`. The throw comes after the
malformed-manifest check and before any `deriveStatus`, executor call or log. Its message is pinned verbatim:

`tier <tier>: the fallback switch is the PR tier's (§13.8's pre-decided fallback; the nightly tier absorbs the difference) — tier:<tier> runs at its own sizes; run it without the fallback`

* The CLI's own refusal and its text are unchanged (`index.ts` is byte-equal to its blob).
* No export was added, removed or renamed.
* A thrown `Error` is `runTier`'s existing refusal form (the malformed manifest throws the same way), so it counts as
  the "typed, pinned" refusal the row asks for. The message is pinned verbatim by the test.

**No lawful caller needs the switch elsewhere.** A grep of `bench/src`, `packages/*/src` and `tools` for `runTier` and
`fallback` finds exactly two callers outside the folder (CONFIRMED by grep, PLAUSIBLE that no future caller needs it):

* `tier-jobs/cli.ts:757`, the receipt: `runTier(rm.manifest, { root, out: dir, mode: 'plain', log, … })`, with no
  `fallback`;
* `timing-phase/tiers.ts:120`: `{ ...c.options, root, out, mode, exec, log }`, with no `fallback` set anywhere.

**Pins.**

* `runner.test.ts` 'Q175 (d): runTier refuses the fallback switch on a tier:%s manifest …', over nightly and
  milestone. In plain, whole and batched mode it expects an `Error`, the message verbatim, no executor call, no probe
  call (a harness job is listed first) and an empty out folder. With `fallback: false`, or with the switch omitted,
  the same manifest runs at its own sizes.
* 'Q175 (d): tier:pr keeps the switch in every mode'.
* The earlier fallback tests are unchanged (CONFIRMED by the diff).

**Mutants.** All ran in the mirror against NEAR. Every one is red:

| G1 | the guard removed (behaviourally the before-image: it differs from the index blob in comments only) | both refusal tests, 'expected null to be an instance of Error' |
| G2 | refuse every tier, pr too | 5 tests (the pr fallback pins of exec.test.ts and runner.test.ts) |

## The refusal census (J264, N-58). CONFIRMED

The item's registered families were run through `runTier` in the mirror: the three real manifests
(`tier-jobs/index.ts` `manifest(tier, PLAT_ROOT)`), with a no-op executor and a probe that answers true, for each tier
and each value of the switch (undefined, false, true). The census ran before (G1's `runner.ts`, the before-image) and
after (the tree's `runner.ts`). The probe folder `bench/test/zzcensus` was deleted afterwards and `runner.ts` restored
(`cmp` equal to the tree).

| tier | switch omitted or false (before = after) | switch true, before | switch true, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| pr | ran, 62 units, 10 jobs, 1 pending | ran, 58 units, 3 sizes cut | ran, 58 units, 3 sizes cut |
| nightly | ran, 169 units, 1 pending, 1 not built | ran, 55 units, 3 sizes cut | **REFUSED** (the message verbatim) |
| milestone | ran, 170 units, 1 pending | ran, 56 units, 3 sizes cut | **REFUSED** (the message verbatim) |

* Lawful-input refusals: 0 → 0.
* The two new refusals are UNLAWFUL input: §13.8 states the fallback for the PR tier only ("the nightly tier absorbs
  the difference").
* Their verdict is REFUSE, typed and visible: a thrown `Error` before anything runs.
* The alternative is named in the message (run the tier without the fallback). No user reaches the class through
  §11.4's doors, because the command line refuses `--fallback` first with exit 64.
* The census did not rise for any lawful class.

One non-blocking note, recorded in `checks/M0-f-02a-notes.md`:

* **N-15, a truthy non-boolean `fallback` passes the guard (deliberate-writer escape; M4). CONFIRMED by a mirror
  probe.** `runTier(nightlyManifest, { fallback: 1 as unknown as boolean })` RAN, and so did `'yes'`. The guard tests
  `=== true`, but `applyFallback` takes any truthy value, so fuzz 10 000 → 5 000 was applied and recorded as
  `fallback.applied: 1` / `"yes"`. `true` was REFUSED. Only a caller that defeats the `boolean` type can reach this,
  and the record shows it, so it fails visibly. A manifest relabelled `tier: 'pr'` that carries the nightly jobs also
  passes, again only by a deliberate writer.
